acceptance_evidence: AC1, a red that exits 0 is refused and still recorded: RedRuleTest covers the refusal and that the record is appended anyway
AC2, a timeout and a command that could not start are refused as RED evidence: two tests, one per exit code
AC3, a slice citing a red that passed is refused: CitedRedTest builds such a record directly and the gate rejects it

AC4, advance is refused without a coverage measurement and with a negative delta, and a first measurement passes with a null delta: four tests in CoverageTest, and record 17 is the real measurement on this tree at 100% of lines
AC5, a blocking decision that did not clear says so: RefusalMessageTest asserts both directions, since must_fix refuses when it clears
AC6, return appends a rework record: covered by the SEEN-086 lifecycle tests and exercised for real on this ticket at records 24 of SEEN-006 and 15 of SEEN-088

findings.claim: Writing the coverage baseline at delivery changed the tree the receipt had just attested
findings.failure_scenario: Every delivery from here on writes docs/harness/coverage.json after taking the fingerprint, so the receipt attests a tree that no longer exists by the time the command returns, and the next verify-delivery on the same branch refuses. It is the circularity ADR 0002 exists to resolve, reintroduced by a file nobody thought of as evidence
findings.resolution: The baseline is bookkeeping and now sits outside the fingerprint beside the journal, the drafts and the graph, with a test asserting it. Caught by the regression check in this ticket's own tdd stage, which then refused the advance

findings.claim: Enforcing the RED rule invalidated fixtures written before it existed
findings.failure_scenario: Three older gate tests built synthetic red records with exit 0, so they would have passed a rule they were meant to exercise and hidden a regression in it
findings.resolution: The fixture now fails a red by default. Correcting fixtures rather than the rule was the right way round: the tests encoded an assumption that a phase label alone made a red

findings.claim: The coverage gate applies to packages/core only, while five packages carry placeholder tests
findings.failure_scenario: A later ticket adds real code to packages/connectors or packages/agent with no tests, and nothing notices, because the floor covers one package
findings.resolution: Deliberate and recorded in the solution: a floor under placeholder tests measures nothing while looking like a control. The gated set is one line in harness/coverage.py and should grow as each package gains real behaviour, which is a note for the tickets that add it

findings.claim: The coverage baseline file can be edited to make a fall look like a rise
findings.failure_scenario: A session under time pressure edits docs/harness/coverage.json downward and the gate passes on a genuine regression
findings.resolution: Accepted and named in the solution's risks: it is one small committed file, moved only by a delivery, and read in the same diff a reviewer sees. The harness makes it visible rather than impossible, which is the same stance it takes on waivers and overrides

security_checklist: One new dependency, @vitest/coverage-v8, pinned to match the vitest already in the lockfile after the first install pulled a mismatched major
No live marketplace call in any test
No agent action and no policy-gate surface
